title: Three-into-three increase (bobble base)
subtitle: Working three stitches from one to create the foundation of a bobble or popcorn.
excerpt: The three-into-three increase (abbreviated 3-in-3) works a knit, a yarn over, and a knit into the same stitch, turning one stitch into three. It is the standard base method for five-stitch bobbles and popcorn textures in Aran and textured knitting.
sourceNotes: Standard increase used in Aran bobble construction. Weldon's Practical Knitter Aran-style volumes and Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938) describe equivalent worked-from-one expansions. Modern UK Aran pattern convention uses this or the k1f&b variant as the bobble foundation.
heroPrompt: Close-up of a knitted swatch showing a raised bobble on a purl background, the bobble formed from a three-into-three increase worked several rows below.

glossaryTerms.definition: An increase worked by knitting, yarn-overing, and knitting again all into the same stitch, producing three stitches from one. Used as the base for bobbles and popcorn textures.
A raised, rounded knitted stitch cluster formed by increasing into one stitch, working several rows short on those extra stitches, then decreasing back to one. Common in Aran and textured knitting.

aliases: knit yarn over knit into one stitch

content.text: works a knit stitch, a yarn over, and a second knit stitch all into the same base stitch without slipping it off the needle until all three have been formed. The result is a small cluster of three live stitches, which the pattern then uses as the base for a
. The same move forms the foundation of popcorn and puff stitches in Aran knitting. Difficulty: intermediate.
Needles in the correct size for the yarn weight
A practice swatch of at least 15 stitches worked in reverse stocking stitch (purl on RS) as the background
Work to the bobble stitch. This is the single stitch that will be expanded into three.

Insert the right needle into the stitch as if to knit. Wrap the yarn and draw a loop through, but do not slide the original stitch off the left needle. You now have one new stitch on the right needle and the original stitch still on the left.
Bring the yarn over the top of the right needle to the front (yarn over). This creates the second of the three new stitches on the right needle.
Insert the right needle into the same original stitch again as if to knit. Wrap the yarn and draw a loop through. Now slide the original stitch off the left needle.

Three stitches now sit on the right needle where one existed before. The pattern will now typically turn the work and work several short rows on these three stitches, then decrease back to one, to form the full bobble.

attrs.title: Completing the bobble
attrs.body: After the 3-in-3 increase, a standard five-stitch bobble turns the work and purls across the three, turns again and knits, then turns and purls once more before working k3tog (or sl1, k2tog, psso) to return to one stitch. The exact bobble completion sequence varies by pattern; always follow the pattern's own instructions.

content.text: The three-into-three increase appears in Aran patterns wherever a bobble or popcorn sits on the stitch chart. It also forms the base for the five-into-five increase used in larger bobbles. Any Aran pattern that reads "make bobble (mb)" will define the bobble in its abbreviations; the 3-in-3 or a similar worked-from-one sequence is usually the method used.

items.symptom: The original stitch slips off the left needle before all three new stitches are made
items.cause: The needle was withdrawn too far between steps
items.fix: Hold the base stitch firmly on the left needle after each insertion. Only slide the original stitch off after the third and final loop has been drawn through.

items.symptom: The yarn over forms too loose a stitch
items.cause: The yarn over was wrapped in the wrong direction or too loosely
items.fix: Bring the yarn over the top of the right needle from back to front. Keep the tension consistent with the surrounding stitches by holding the yarn snug.

items.symptom: The bobble does not stand proud of the fabric
items.cause: Not enough turning rows were worked on the three stitches, or the bobble was worked in stocking rather than reverse stocking stitch background
items.fix: Follow the pattern's turning-row count exactly. Bobbles pop out most on a reverse stocking stitch (purl) background.
